bridge_street._note: San Anselmo Creek at Bridge Street = Marin OneRain 'FS 19' (site 38036) = NWS/NWPS 'SBSC1'. Same gauge/datum; flood cats action 11.3 / minor 13.3 / moderate 16.3 / major 17.8 ft.

town_stages._note: Town of San Anselmo 'Emergency Procedures in Event of Winter Storms and Flooding', 2013 staff report (sananselmo.gov ArchiveCenter Item/3152). Five operational stages on the downtown Station 19 / Bridge St gauge. Stage 1 is a pre-storm forecast condition with no creek level. 13 ft = water reaches the building at 730 San Anselmo Ave.
town_stages.stage1_note: Large storms forecast + ground saturated: alert merchants, stage sand & bags, first staff alert

sump._note: Two PumpFuse PF03 units (ESP32/Espressif), identified on the LAN by MAC (kept out of this public repo). The PF03 exposes NO local API: the reachable unit had zero open TCP ports (full 1-1024 + IoT scan), no mDNS/Bonjour advert, no Tuya broadcast; the manufacturer confirms cloud-only operation. So there is nothing to poll locally today. Set each pump's 'url' to a JSON endpoint once one exists - a future PF03 local REST endpoint, or a bridge (Home Assistant, an MQTT->HTTP shim, or a cloud export). Env overrides: SUMP_PRIMARY_URL, SUMP_BACKUP_URL. Empty url = disabled. PumpFuse is energy-based (no pit-level sensor); it reports on/off, watts, runtime, cycles, gallons.
sump._geometry_note: A 36-inch pit holds 4.4064 gal per inch of depth, so delivered GPM = float_differential_in * 18.885 (~x19). At the assumed 4.5 in that is 84.98 GPM, within 1.2% of the 84 GPM nameplate - an independent check on the pump rating from geometry alone. But the differential is ASSUMED: at 4.0 in delivered drops to 75.5 GPM and at 3.0 in to 56.7 GPM. Every inflow, gallons and stress figure in analysis/ scales linearly with this number. Measure it before trusting any of them.
sump._note2: gpm here is mirrored from primary_pump/backup_pump.rated_gpm, which are the single source of truth. Do not edit these two numbers directly - change the spec block below and mirror. The old 40/30 placeholders were wrong and have been removed.

_pump_spec_note: Nameplate specs for the two pumps - the single source of truth for GPM. sump.pumps[].gpm mirrors rated_gpm and sump.pumps[].spec names the block it mirrors. Measured draw over 3,674 runs (Sep 2025-Jun 2026) averaged 1394 W against the 1380 W rating, so the primary runs at its rated duty point and 84 GPM is the right constant for inflow. 'hp' was dropped: the old 1.0/0.75 values did not match these models and no verified figure replaced them.

thresholds._note: SUPERSEDED by the 'tiers' block below, kept only so old history.csv rows stay interpretable. Replayed against winter 2025-26 these rules fired nothing at all on 8 of 15 storms, including the largest (5.54 in, Bridge St 7.38 ft). See analysis/report.md.

qpf_bias._note: Open-Meteo runs dry here. Measured against station totals over Nov 2025-Apr 2026: day-ahead QPF captured 75.5% of observed rain, 3-day lead 49.6%, and the five wettest events were under-forecast 41% and 68%. Every QPF used in a rule is multiplied by these before comparison.

creek_predictor._note: Layer 3A, Bridge Street stage on the rising limb only (n=349 observed readings). Used by the Act tier: feed r6h_in = observed last-6h rain + bias-corrected next-6h QPF, and api = current antecedent index. Season-to-date was dropped - it added +0.005 R2 across every layer tested.

ross_to_bridge._note: Peak-to-peak fit across 24 storms, R2 0.9965, residual sd 0.0967 ft. Ross (USGS 11460000) is real-time and reliable; Bridge Street's own gauge is event-based and sparse. The notify line sits INSIDE the fitted range, the flood lines do not.

tiers._note: Rebuilt 2026-09-08 from the winter 2025-26 replay. Ordered quiet < watch < prepare < act < emergency; the highest satisfied rule wins. 'ross_ft' is USGS 11460000 stage, 'bridge_ft' is San Anselmo at Bridge St, 'run_s' is a single primary-pump run length. QPF terms are already bias-corrected by qpf_bias.

act._escalation_note: The bare 3-increasing-runs rule fires on 2.6% of all runs (94 triggers, 21 days) and 78 of those 94 land on runs still under 25 s - a 62% false-alarm rate at Act. Requiring the third run to be at least 25 s cuts it to 16 triggers on 8 days while keeping every real storm.
